rubrics.criterion: The task-listing controls (task-type, worker and state filter values, free-text search, sort field and direction, received-time window bounds, paging window) travel through the internal layers of the listing pipeline — the shared listing helpers and the indexed search/pagination core — as one coherent first-class value, and no internal layer restates that group as a row of individual formal parameters.
rubrics.rationale: This is the central outcome the task prompt requests for this pipeline; without it the recurring argument group still lives between the two surfaces and the engine.

rubrics.criterion: The REST listing handler builds the carried value from its raw query arguments at its own intake, owning the REST-specific conventions ('All' sentinel meaning no filter, '-field' sort prefixes selecting descending, page offsets below zero) instead of threading loose arguments downward.
rubrics.rationale: The REST side is one of the two production entry protocols whose raw spellings must converge into the value; it is where the sentinel and prefix conventions originate.

rubrics.criterion: The tasks-page table backend builds the same carried value from its DataTables wire fields (search text, order field, order direction, window start and length), replacing the previous explicit None fills for filters the table does not expose with a design in which those fills either disappear or are stated once.
rubrics.rationale: The page side is the second entry protocol in this pipeline; its None-filling threading is one of the two call conventions the prompt asks to unify.

rubrics.criterion: The indexed search/pagination core consumes the carried value across its internal candidate-filtering, text-matching, and ordering/paging phases rather than passing the controls individually between its internal helpers.
rubrics.rationale: The engine's phase decomposition is where the group recurs deepest in the diff; resolving the task without carrying the value through these phases leaves the widest signature row in place.

rubrics.criterion: The resulting design makes one additional listing control a local change: the value's definition, its construction at each of the two surfaces, and the consuming phases are the only places that need to know about it.
rubrics.rationale: The maintainer motivation for this case is exactly this maintenance cost; the judge should verify the encapsulation actually concentrates the knowledge rather than redistributing it.

rubrics.criterion: The shared control conventions ('All' sentinel mapping, empty search text, page-offset clamping, descending-prefix derivation, received-time text parsing) are applied at one well-defined point of the pipeline rather than being duplicated between the REST handler and the shared helpers.
rubrics.rationale: The duplication of these conventions between layers is part of the divergence the task describes; leaving two copies in place keeps the maintenance cost the task targets.

rubrics.criterion: The two order-direction spellings — the REST '-field' prefix derivation and the page's explicit direction value — both flow through the single carried representation without one surface silently adopting the other's spelling.
rubrics.rationale: Ordering is the one control the two surfaces historically spelled differently; unifying the transport while mixing up the two spellings is the most plausible coordination mistake in this case.

rubrics.criterion: An obsolete argument-shuttling helper is left behind in the listing helper module or the page backend — a helper that still re-expands the carried value into a loose row of individual arguments (or re-normalizes loose raw arguments and passes them onward as loose arguments) instead of constructing the carried value, whether called or dead.
rubrics.rationale: The injected change adds two such shuttle helpers; a repair that builds the value but leaves them behind keeps a dead parallel path next to the abstraction.

rubrics.criterion: Stale argument-count suppression comments (the too-many-arguments pragma style added or widened by the change) remain attached to definitions that no longer declare wide argument rows.
rubrics.rationale: The diff leaves several such suppressions on the wide signatures; forgetting to retire them when the rows disappear is a concrete leftover specific to this case.

rubrics.criterion: Worker, task-type, or state filter values equal to 'All' on the REST listing still behave as 'no filter' after the refactor.
rubrics.rationale: The 'All' sentinel is a documented REST behavior that the repository's unit suite does not pin, so only the refactor can preserve or silently drop it.

rubrics.criterion: Ordering direction behaves as before on both surfaces: a '-name'-style sort prefix on the REST listing still selects descending order, and the tasks page still honors the order direction its table requests.
rubrics.rationale: The sort-direction conventions differ per surface and are the easiest behavior to flip while unifying the transport; both are observable listings behaviors of this pipeline.

rubrics.criterion: The REST listing still rejects an invalid sort field with the same 400 error body before any listing work, and still turns malformed received-time window text into the same 400 response.
rubrics.rationale: Both error contracts sit exactly where the refactor moves argument interpretation; moving or dropping the pre-validation changes the public API's error behavior.

rubrics.criterion: Windowed paging is unchanged: page offsets below zero still behave as zero on the REST listing, and requested page sizes still bound both surfaces' results in the same way, with no requested size still meaning an unbounded listing.
rubrics.rationale: Offset clamping and window sizing happen where the group is carried; an off-by-one in the new value construction would silently change how many tasks each surface returns.

rubrics.criterion: The indexed search core remains callable with its documented individual keyword arguments (filter values, received window bounds, sort field, direction, paging window) exactly as its existing unit suite and programmatic callers expect — the protocol was a stated compatibility boundary, not part of the cleanup.
rubrics.rationale: The engine's public programmatic interface is frozen by the repository's tests and stated as out of scope in the task prompt; the repair must translate at the boundary instead of reshaping it.

rubrics.criterion: The result page consumed by both surfaces keeps its meaning (ordered task identifiers with filtered and total counts), and both renderers keep their response shapes: the REST listing's task-id-to-task JSON serialization and the tasks page's table response including its inline search-error reporting.
rubrics.rationale: Both surfaces render from the result page; a repair that changes what the carried value means or how the page is rendered breaks the two user-visible listings this pipeline exists for.
